newsitem.title: CANADA: Air Canada to deploy combis on Atlantic.
newsitem.headline: Air Canada to deploy combis on Atlantic.

text.p: Air Canada will become an all bellyhold cargo operator on transpacific routes by mid-summer with the shift of its Boeing 747-400 combis back to North Atlantic routes, a company official said.
With the redeployment, Air Canada will offer some main-deck freight capacity for the April-October schedule from three of its major Western European gateways - London, Paris and Zurich.
The carrier has used 747 combis on both the Seoul and Hong Kong routes. It dropped the combis on Seoul last year after finding it could not attract sufficient high yielding traffic.

Air Canada's Hong Kong cargo traffic is much stronger, but because of the distance involved, the airline's 747-400 combi - which have a range limit of 6,600 miles - often could only carry 15-20 tonnes, compared with a rated capacity of 39 tonnes, the official said.

The 747's replacement on Vancouver-Hong Kong is the high gross weight version of the Airbus Industrie 340-300, with a 7,300 mile range. To Hong Kong, the smaller A340 ends up carrying the same amount of cargo - bellyhold only - and almost as many passengers for operating costs 40 percent less than a 747 combi.
The redeployment means Air Canada could have as many as six 747 combis on the North Atlantic for next fall's cargo peak, where they can carry a full cargo load.

The official said the redeployment is timely because 1997 has been a strong year so far on the North Atlantic, with ex-Paris loads in particular showing renewed vigor. Capacity on Toronto-Paris has tightened with the withdrawal late last year of Canadian Airlines International.
Also this summer, Air Canada plans to serve Calgary-Frankfurt with an A340 rather than the smaller B-767-300. -Air Cargo Newsroom Tel +44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
